claims.claim: Cold starts on the consumption plan can take more than 2 seconds on their own
claims.about: C# / .NET on Azure Functions consumption plan
claims.measured: csharp-aspnet start-up 785 ms (ASP.NET Core in Docker, not Azure Functions)
claims.why: The benchmark times an ASP.NET Core container start on fixed hardware, which leaves out what a consumption-plan cold start includes: allocating an instance, loading the Functions host and starting the isolated worker.

claims.claim: docs/team-notes.md suggests writing new functions in Node or Go because of .NET start-up time, which implies .NET starts more slowly than Node or Go
claims.measured: csharp-aspnet 785 ms vs node-express 706 ms, node-fastify 593 ms, go-nethttp 238 ms, go-gin 293 ms
claims.why: In the measurements .NET does start more slowly: about 3x slower than Go and only slightly slower than Node (785 ms vs 593–706 ms), so the direction is right even though the gap to Node is small.
